world: The Fjord — cold blue-black ground from fjord depth; an absolute waterline as the only structural rule; one warm value (brass, low sun on water) reserved for the active state and primary action. Scandinavian restraint: craft in the joinery, no applied ornament.
medium: authored as HTML/CSS in the shipping medium, then rasterised with qlmanage
prompt: Not a generated image. This machine reports no image generation (context.mjs: converters only, cwebp/sips), so the comp round was run in the medium the product actually ships — real HTML/CSS at app viewport — and rasterised for the record. The substitution was disclosed to the user before approval. Source of truth for each comp is its .html sibling.
concept: The Sound — a channel between two walls. Full album hero with art at real size, track list as the channel, watch as the far wall whose water level is the capacity.

approval.decided: F as the base, with G's now-playing treatment folded into the album hero.
carry_forward: F's three-column topology: sources/playlists rail, album channel, watch wall
F's album hero: art at real size with HiFi metadata beside it
G's now-playing treatment: large art, big title, format badge
E's downward-send gesture, kept as a behaviour rather than a layout
do_not_literalize: The 'bit-perfect' badge. Webview audio goes through CoreAudio's mixer and may resample; unverified, and must not ship as a claim until it is.
The .cover gradients are value stand-ins, not artwork. Real embedded art replaces them.
The 1180x760 frame is a north star for composition, not a fixed layout. The build is responsive.
Free space, track counts and file sizes are real values read off the FR165 — keep them real, never invent replacements.
